semantic_fragments.content: 红外体温计是通过使用红外传感器, 在不接触额头的情况下, 接收额头温度所辐射出的红外线信号，来计算人体温度。红外传感器可接收额头温度所辐射出的红外线信号, 并转换成感应电压, 通过测量该感应电压,并经过计算处理修正后, 将测量温度以数字的形式通过LCD显示器显示出测量体温值。

9.设计输入评审时，项目组和使用者代表需用批判的眼光评审被提议的要求，识别出项目组对客户需求作出公开的和暗指的错误的假定，以避免引起严重的错误后果；
10.设计输入评审需形成评审记录；
11.评审后的设计输入在放行前需得到批准，批准信息要包括批准人签字和批准日期。

组织和技术接口：软件工程师负责拟制、软件主管负责审核软件构建与编码。
工作流程：1.软件工程师拟制"软件构建与编码"提交软件主管审核；2.软件工程师设计并输出软件代码文件，提交软件主管审核；3.软件工程师拟制"软件测试计划"，提交软件主管审核及技术负责人批准；4.软件工程师依据"软件测试计划"进行子程序测试及软件系统测试，并形成"子程序测试记录"和"软件系统测试记录"；5.软件工程师将"子程序测试记录"和"软件系统测试记录"提交软件主管审核；6.软件工程师将审核后的软件代码文件、"子程序测试记录"、"软件系统测试记录"和批准后的"软件测试计划"提交技术负责人；7.技术负责人批准软件代码文件。

semantic_fragments.content: 质量要求（6.19 T1样机制作）：1.本阶段的设计验证需证明T1样机阶段的通用要求部分、功能规格部分、性能规格部分、组件规格部分和法规标准清单部分等设计输出需满足设计输入的要求；2.本阶段的设计验证还需证明T1样机的安全性和有效性；3.设计验证必须依据设计验证计划进行，该计划在放行前需得到批准，批准信息要包括批准人签字和批准日期；4.设计验证计划需包括验证阶段、验证内容、接收准则、验证人员、人员职责、验证日期等；5.设计验证行为需形成设计验证报告；6.设计验证报告需包括验证内容、验证方法、验证结论、验证日期及验证人员等；7.为保证数据的可靠性，验证用的测试设备需经过校正和控制；8.设计验证需要进行评审，用以检查验证的完整性和适宜性。

semantic_fragments.content: 组织和技术接口（6.19 T1样机制作）：软件工程师、硬件工程师、结构工程师负责装配制作T1样机。详细流程：1.外协模具厂在模具制造完成后，按照图纸中的材质、颜色要求生产T1塑料件，提供给资源开发工程师；2.资源开发工程师提交"样品验判单"、T1塑料件给品质工程师、结构工程师进行样品验判；3.样品验判完成后，结构工程师组织将T1塑料件、外观图进行塑料件丝印；4.结构工程师依据总装类、辅料类组件清单提供结构件，软件工程师、硬件工程师依据机芯类组件清单提供机芯，由工程师和相关人员组装T1样机；5.项目负责人组织各专业工程师依据批准后的"设计验证计划-通用要求部分"进行设计验证，并形成T1样机"设计验证报告-通用要求部分"；6.项目负责人将T1样机"设计验证报告-通用要求部分"提交软件主管、硬件主管、结构主管审核；7.软件工程师依据批准后的"产品检验标准"和"设计验证计划-功能规格部分"进行设计验证，并形成T1样机"设计验证报告-功能规格部分"；8.软件工程师将T1样机"设计验证报告-功能规格部分"提交软件主管审核；9.专业工程师提交T1样机进行相关实验，并汇总收集实验报告；10.硬件工程师依据批准后的"产品检验标准"和"设计验证计划-性能规格部分"进行电池使用寿命测试并形成"电池使用寿命测试报告"；11.硬件工程师依据批准后的"产品检验标准"和"设计验证计划-性能规格部分"进行设计验证，并形成T1样机"设计验证报告-性能规格部分"；12.硬件工程师将T1样机"设计验证报告-性能规格部分"、"电池使用寿命测试/评估报告"提交硬件主管审核；13.结构工程师依据批准后的"产品检验标准"和"设计验证计划-组件规格部分"进行设计验证，并形成T1样机"设计验证报告-组件规格部分"；14.结构工程师将T1样机"设计验证报告-组件规格部分"提交结构主管审核；15.项目负责人将审核后的"设计验证报告-通用要求部分"、"设计验证报告-功能规格部分"、"设计验证报告-性能规格部分"汇总，共同形成T1样机"设计验证报告"。

semantic_fragments.content: 质量要求（设计更改通用）：1.设计更改需求部门提出更改要求或需要纠正的问题；2.技术人员需要对设计更改需求进行评审，以确定拒绝、延期或接受更改要求；3.对设计更改需求进行评审，还要识别是设计确认前的更改还是设计确认后的更改。若是设计确认前的更改，且对预期用途、设计输入无影响，即只影响设计输出，在阶段设计评审时需要进行设计更改影响的评估；4.设计更改时需要对更改原因、纠正措施、更改计划以及设计更改对设计输入要求和预期使用目的的影响等进行充分的可行性评估；5.对于设计确认后的设计更改需要进行再验证和/或再确认，以保障设计更改满足制造或客户需求；6.设计更改需要进行风险管理，以保证即解决原有问题，同时不引起新的问题；或者如果引起了新的问题，会对这些问题进行追踪，直至解决；7.更新设计文档，以确切反映已进行修改的设计。

semantic_fragments.content: 设计更改（设计确认后）主要工作内容：1.设计更改需求部门提出更改要求或需要纠正的问题；2.技术人员需要对设计更改需求进行评审，以确定拒绝、延期或接受更改要求；3.对设计更改需求进行评审，还要识别是设计确认前的更改还是设计确认后的更改。若是设计确认前的更改，且对预期用途、设计输入无影响，即只影响设计输出，在阶段设计评审时需要进行设计更改影响的评估；4.设计更改时需要对更改原因、纠正措施、更改计划以及设计更改对设计输入要求和预期使用目的的影响等进行充分的可行性评估；5.对于设计确认后的设计更改需要进行再验证和/或再确认，以保障设计更改满足制造或客户需求；6.设计更改需要进行风险管理，以保证即解决原有问题，同时不引起新的问题；或者如果引起了新的问题，会对这些问题进行追踪，直至解决；7.更新设计文档，以确切反映已进行修改的设计。

semantic_fragments.content: The risk management process will be conducted in accordance with standard ISO 14971:2019, EN ISO 14971:2019 and EN ISO 14971:2019/A11:2021. The risk management plan covers the whole life-cycle of the medical device across the following phases: (1) Initial development: document intended use and reasonably foreseeable misuse, identify characteristics related to safety, identify hazards and hazardous situations, estimate risks, evaluate risks, draft risk control measures plan. Output: Report of risk assessment. (2) Prototype phase (Design verification): verify implementation and effectiveness of risk control measures, assess residual risk, make benefit-risk analysis, evaluate risks arising from risk control measures, review completeness of risk control. Output: Report of verification of risk control measure and residual risk evaluation. (3) Design validation: overall residual risk evaluation, form the risk management report. Output: Report of risk management. (4) Design change: identify hazards from design change, evaluate and assess risks, draft and verify risk control measures plan, assess residual risk, benefit-risk analysis, overall residual risk evaluation after design change. Outputs: Record of risk evaluation, Report of verification of risk control measure and residual risk evaluation in design change, Report of Risk Management in design change. (5) Production and post-production activities: collect production and post-production information, assess for new or previously unidentified hazards, analyze risks and make control plans if necessary, track implementation of risk control measures. Reference: Risk Management Control Regulation (QI-7.3-22) section 4.11.1. Output: Report of Post-market Risk Management.

semantic_fragments.content:
Risk Acceptance Criteria (Section 3.3): A risk matrix is defined with Probability Classes (1–6) on one axis and Severity Classes (1–5) on the other axis. Two zones are defined:
- Not acceptable: Unacceptable risk. Risk control measures are required.
- Acceptable: Insignificant/negligible risk. No risk control measures are required.

The manufacturer shall reduce the risk as far as possible using one or more of the following risk control options in the priority order listed:
(a) Eliminate or reduce risks as far as possible through safe design and manufacture;
(b) Where appropriate, take adequate protection measures, including alarms if necessary, in relation to risks that cannot be eliminated;
(c) Provide information for safety (warnings/precautions/contra-indications) and, where appropriate, training to users.

semantic_fragments.content: Residual Risk Acceptance Criteria (Section 4.1 - For Single Residual Risk): When a risk falls in the 'Not acceptable' area, risk control measures must be taken. After taking measures, the risk becomes a residual risk. If this residual risk still falls in the 'Not acceptable' area per the criteria in Section 3.3, a risk-benefit analysis must be conducted. This residual risk will be acceptable when there are reasonable reasons to support that the benefits outweigh the risks.

semantic_fragments.content:
For Overall Residual Risk:
1. The benefits related to the intended use of the medical device are weighed against the overall residual risk. Benefits can be described by their magnitude or extent, the probability of experiencing the benefit within the intended patient populations, and the duration and frequency of the benefit. The evaluation may take into account knowledge of the intended medical indication, the generally acknowledged state of the art in technology and medicine, and the availability of alternative medical devices or treatments.
2. Visual representations of the residual risks can be useful. Each individual residual risk can be shown in a risk matrix as shown in section 3.3. If more than 1/2 of the risks are in the higher severity regions or in the higher probability regions of the risk matrix, or clusters of risks are borderline, then the distribution of the risks can indicate that the overall residual risk might not be acceptable, even if each individual risk has been judged acceptable.
3. Overall risk-benefit analysis: when the benefits outweigh the overall residual risks, the overall residual risks are acceptable.
4. If the overall residual risks are acceptable after evaluation, then the significant residual risks shall be notified to the users and involve the information in the accompanying documents. If the overall residual risks are not acceptable after evaluation, then additional risk control measures shall be taken, or the modification to the medical devices may be required.

semantic_fragments.content:
Risk Management Activities by Phase:

1. Initial development: (1) Document intended use and reasonably foreseeable misuse; (2) Identify characteristics related to safety; (3) Identify hazards and hazardous situations; (4) Estimate the risk(s) of each hazardous situation; (5) Risk evaluation; (6) Draft the risk control measures plan. Responsibility: Project manager organizes; members review. Output: Report of risk assessment.

2. Prototype phase (Design verification): (1) Verify implementation and effectiveness of risk control measures plan; (2) Assess residual risk; (3) Make benefit-risk analysis; (4) Evaluate whether there are any risks arising from risk control measures; (5) Review completeness of risk control. Responsibility: Project manager organizes; members review. Output: Report of verification of risk control measure and residual risk evaluation.

3. Design validation: (1) Overall residual risk evaluation; (2) Form the risk management report. Responsibility: Project manager organizes; members review. Output: Report of risk management.

4. Design change: (1) Identify hazards and hazardous situations related to design change; (2) Evaluate risk(s) in hazardous situation resulting from design change; (3) Assess risk(s) in design change; (4) Draft the plan of risk control measures for design change; (5) Verify the implementation of plan on risk control measures after design change; (6) Assess residual risk, benefit-risk analysis and any new risks after design change; (7) Overall residual risk evaluation after design change. Responsibility: Project manager organizes; members review. Output: Record of risk evaluation (when no new risk); Report of verification of risk control measure and residual risk evaluation in design change; Report of Risk Management in design change.

5. Production and post-production activities: (1) Collect information concerning production and post-production; (2) Assess if there are hazards or hazardous situations not identified before, and if the risk(s) become not acceptable; whether the overall residual risk is still acceptable in relation to the benefits of the intended use; and whether the generally acknowledged state of the art has changed; (3) Analyze and assess the risk(s) and make risk control plan and actions if necessary; (4) Track the implementation of risk control measures. Reference: Section 4.11.1 of Risk Management Control Regulation (QI-7.3-22). Output: Report of Post-market Risk Management.

semantic_fragments.content: Residual Risk Acceptance Criteria - Overall Residual Risk: (1) Benefits related to intended use are weighed against overall residual risk, considering magnitude, probability, duration and frequency of benefit, intended medical indication, state of the art, and availability of alternatives. (3) Overall risk-benefit analysis: when benefits outweigh overall residual risks, overall residual risks are acceptable. (4) If overall residual risks are acceptable, significant residual risks shall be notified to users in accompanying documents. If not acceptable, additional risk control measures shall be taken or modification to the medical device may be required.

Design change: Identify hazards related to design change; evaluate risks from design change; assess risks; draft risk control measures plan; verify implementation; assess residual risk, benefit-risk analysis and new risks; overall residual risk evaluation after design change. For Overall Residual Risk:
1. The benefits related to the intended use of the medical device are weighed against the overall residual risk. Benefits can be described by their magnitude or extent, the probability of experiencing the benefit within the intended patient populations, and the duration and frequency of the benefit. The evaluation may take into account knowledge of the intended medical indication, the generally acknowledged state of the art in technology and medicine, and the availability of alternative medical devices or treatments.
2. Visual representations of the residual risks can be useful. Each individual residual risk can be shown in a risk matrix as shown in section 3.3. If more than 1/2 of the risks are in the higher severity regions or in the higher probability regions of the risk matrix, or clusters of risks are borderline, then the distribution of the risks can indicate that the overall residual risk might not be acceptable, even if each individual risk has been judged acceptable.
3. Overall risk-benefit analysis: when the benefits outweigh the overall residual risks, the overall residual risks are acceptable.
4. If the overall residual risks are acceptable after evaluation, then the significant residual risks shall be notified to the users and involve the information in the accompanying documents. If the overall residual risks are not acceptable after evaluation, then additional risk control measures shall be taken, or the modification to the medical devices may be required.

semantic_fragments.content: Risk Acceptance Criteria: A risk matrix is used combining Severity (1-5) and Probability (1-6). Risks are classified as either 'Not acceptable' (unacceptable risk, risk control measures are required) or 'Acceptable' (insignificant/negligible risk, no risk control measures required). The manufacturer shall reduce risk as far as possible using the following risk control options in priority order: (a) eliminate or reduce risks as far as possible through safe design and manufacture; (b) where appropriate, take adequate protection measures, including alarms if necessary, in relation to risks that cannot be eliminated; (c) provide information for safety (warnings/precautions/contra-indications) and, where appropriate, training to users.

semantic_fragments.content: Residual Risk Acceptance Criteria for Single Residual Risk: When a risk falls in the 'Not acceptable' area, risk control measures must be taken. The residual risk will be acceptable when there are reasonable reasons to support that the benefits outweigh the risks.

IEC 60601-1-2:2014+A1:2020 edition 4.1 补充问题解答（片段6/9）：
- 非ME设备：ME系统中无非ME设备。
- 配置测试：不同系列产品分别测试；同系列产品（电路相似、功能相似）选取能覆盖综合电路和功能的产品进行测试。
- 排除环境：不能在活跃HF外科设备附近及MRI系统RF屏蔽室附近使用，该区域EM干扰强度高。
- 免疫测试通过/失败准则（基本安全）：可接触部件包括应用部分的爬电距离和空气间隙、介电强度、泄漏电流及患者辅助电流测量。
- 工作模式：发射测试时EUT配置为最高可能发射水平；免疫测试时EUT配置为对被测现象具有最高可能敏感性，测试条件参照使用说明书。
- 预期使用环境：专业医疗机构环境和家庭医疗保健环境，不会改变标准中规定的合理可预见EM干扰水平；电磁免疫测试按用户手册定义的体温计进行。
- 端口（ENCLOSURE PORT、交流/直流输入端口、PATIENT coupling PORT、SIP/SOP PORT）：设备对特定调制频率或频率范围不敏感，按表格所列频率测试。
- RF无线通信设备近场免疫：无额外频率和通信，参见IFU，按用户手册定义的体温计进行电磁免疫测试。
- 9 kHz至13.56 MHz频率范围内磁场免疫：本产品无对磁场敏感的元件或电路。

- 级别8（很高）：体温计无法运行，丧失基本功能，顾客很不满意。
- 级别7（高）：体温计能运行，但性能下降，顾客很不满意。
- 级别6（中等）：体温计能运行，但丧失部分功能，顾客不满意。
- 级别5（低）：体温计能运行，但部分功能性能下降，顾客有些不满意。
- 级别4（很低）：装配/外观或其他小细节不符合要求，多数顾客（超过75%）发现有缺陷。
- 级别3（轻微）：装配/外观或其他小细节不符合要求，多数顾客（大约50%）发现有缺陷。
- 级别2（很轻微）：装配/外观或其他小细节不符合要求，多数顾客（少于25%）发现有缺陷。
- 级别1（无）：无可识别的影响。

- 级别10（绝对不可能）：没有设计控制，或控制无法探测潜在原因/机制及后续失效模式，探测概率<5%。
- 级别9（极微小）：设计控制探测潜在原因/机制的概率极小（0.15），分析/探测控制的探测能力很弱（任何阶段均不太可能探测到）；虚拟分析与预期实际操作条件不相关。
- 级别8（微小）：设计控制探测概率微小（0.25），在设计冻结后和发布前通过合格/不合格测试进行系统/产品验证/确认（子系统或系统测试含验收准则）。
- 级别7（很少）：设计控制探测概率很低（0.35），在设计冻结后和发布前通过失效测试进行系统/产品验证/确认。
- 级别6（少）：设计控制探测概率低（0.45），在设计冻结后和发布前通过退化测试进行系统/产品验证/确认。
- 级别5（中等）：设计控制探测概率中等（0.55），在设计冻结前通过合格/不合格测试进行系统/产品确认（可靠性测试、开发或确认测试）。
- 级别4（中上）：设计控制探测概率中上（0.65），在设计冻结前通过失效测试进行系统/产品确认。
- 级别3（高）：设计控制探测概率高（0.75），在设计冻结前通过退化测试进行系统/产品确认。
- 级别2（很高）：设计和分析/探测控制具有强探测能力（0.85），虚拟分析与设计冻结前的实际或扩展操作条件高度相关。
- 级别1（几乎肯定）：设计控制几乎肯定能探测到潜在原因/机制及后续失效模式（>95%），失效原因或失效模式通过设计方案完全预防（如经验证的设计标准、最佳实践或通用材料等）。

1. 绝对不可能（Ranking 10，<5%）：没有设计控制，或控制无法探测潜在原因/机制及后续失效模式。
2. 极微小（Ranking 9，0.15）：设计控制探测能力极弱（在任何阶段均不可能探测到）；虚拟分析与预期实际工作条件不相关。
3. 微小（Ranking 8，0.25）：设计冻结后、发布前的系统/产品验证/确认，采用通过/失败测试（如乘坐与操控、运输、评估等子系统或系统测试）。
4. 很少（Ranking 7，0.35）：设计冻结后、发布前的系统/产品验证/确认，采用失效测试（子系统或系统测试直至发生失效，系统交互测试等）。
5. 少（Ranking 6，0.45）：设计冻结后、发布前的系统/产品验证/确认，采用退化测试（耐久性测试后的子系统或系统测试，如功能检查）。
6. 中等（Ranking 5，0.55）：设计冻结前的系统/产品确认（可靠性测试、开发或确认测试），采用通过/失败测试（如性能验收准则、功能检查等）。
7. 中上（Ranking 4，0.65）：设计冻结前的系统/产品确认，采用失效测试（如直到泄漏、屈服、开裂等）。
8. 高（Ranking 3，0.75）：设计冻结前的系统/产品确认，采用退化测试（如数据趋势、前后值对比等）。
9. 很高（Ranking 2，0.85）：设计分析/探测控制具有强探测能力；虚拟分析与设计冻结前的实际或扩展工作条件高度相关。
10. 几乎肯定（Ranking 1，>95%）：失效原因或失效模式完全通过设计方案预防而无法发生（如经验证的设计标准、最佳实践或通用材料等）。

semantic_fragments.content: §801.30 器械标签标注UDI要求的一般例外情形：以下类型的器械可豁免§801.20的要求，无需标注UDI：(1) 在FDA规定的合规日期之前生产和贴标的成品器械，该例外在合规日期后3年到期；(2) FDA已通过法规豁免第820部分良好生产规范要求的I类器械（§§820.180和820.198持续记录要求除外）；(3) 同一版本或型号的单个一次性使用器械，集中分发于同一器械包装中，拟存储至使用时取出，且不用于单独商业分发（植入式器械不适用此例外，且含此类器械的包装仍须标注UDI）；(4) 仅用于研究、教学或化学分析、不用于任何临床用途的器械；(5) §812.3(b)含义内的定制器械；(6) 第812部分含义内的研究性器械；(7) 非用于人类疾病诊断、治疗、缓解、预防或影响人体结构/功能的兽医医疗器械；(8) 拟从美国出口的器械；(9) 由战略国家储备库持有并依§801.128(f)(2)获得例外或替代方案的器械；(10) FDA依FD&C法第514(b)或514(c)条建立或认可绩效标准并在其中规定§801.20例外的器械；(11) 组合产品或便利套件直接容器内包装的器械（前提是组合产品或便利套件的标签上已标注UDI）。(b) 国家药品编码（NDC）号：若组合产品标签上合规标注NDC号，则该组合产品及其§3.2(e)(1)所述单一实体器械成分不受§801.20约束，但其他器械成分仍须标注UDI（§801.30(a)(11)适用情形除外）。(c) 运输容器例外：本规则不要求在任何运输容器上标注UDI。(d) I类器械的UDI不要求包含生产标识符。

semantic_fragments.content: Setup and operating procedures: The patient is an intended operator. The patient can measure and change battery. Temperature measurement process: (1) Remove protective cap before taking a measurement. (2) Position: Aim the probe at the center of the forehead, keep probe ≤1.18 inch (3cm) away, do not touch the forehead, hold perpendicular to forehead. For object temperature, aim at object without touching. (3) Take temperature: Normal measurement mode - gently press measurement button to start. Dynamic measurement mode - press and hold button for 2 seconds to activate; takes multiple measurements for accurate readings especially for moving subjects like infants; progress bar displayed; releasing button before completion means result will not be displayed. (4) Read temperature: Confirmation beep indicates measurement complete. Baby temperature mode: 89.6℉-100.3℉ (32℃-37.9℃) = White display + 1 long beep; 100.4℉-109.2℉ (38.0℃-42.9℃) = Red display + 4 short beeps. Adult temperature mode: 89.6℉-99.4℉ (32℃-37.4℃) = White display; 99.5℉-100.3℉ (37.5℃-37.9℃) = Orange display; 100.4℉-109.2℉ (38.0℃-42.9℃) = Red display.

semantic_fragments.content: When a measurement fails, possible reasons for measurement errors include: 1. Make sure to remove protective cap before taking a measurement; 2. The environment temperature exceeding the operational range of 50℉-104℉(10℃-40℃) or being unstable, causing the screen to display 'Err'; 3. The target temperature being outside the measurement range of 89.6℉-109.2℉(32℃-42.9℃), causing the screen to display '---', the temperature unit symbol, and the measurement mode symbol; 4. Press and hold the measurement button no more than 2 seconds in dynamic measurement mode, causing the screen to display '---', the dynamic measurement mode symbol, the temperature unit symbol, and the measurement mode symbol.

semantic_fragments.content: Selecting modes: The default mode is baby temperature mode. To switch between the three modes: (1) In the measurement state, press the settings button briefly to enter the mode switching state. (2) Press the settings button briefly to cycle through the baby mode, adult mode, and object temperature mode, with corresponding icons displayed on the LCD screen. (3) Press the measurement button to save the current settings and initiate a measurement process. Note: The thermometer turns off automatically after 15 seconds of inaction.
semantic_fragments._source: 11 T1样机/PT9L-operation guide-20240828.via_lo_html.clean.md

semantic_fragments.content: Switching units: (1) Press and hold the measurement button for 8 seconds to enter the unit switching mode. (2) The screen flashes the current unit. Press the measurement button to toggle between ℃ and ℉, then selected unit will flash, accompanied by a short beep. (3) Press and hold the measurement button for 2 seconds to confirm the setting, the current unit ℃ or ℉ will light up for 3 seconds, accompanied by a short beep. And then the thermometer turns off automatically. Note: The thermometer will automatically turn off after 15 seconds of inactivity, and the selected unit will also be saved automatically even if without pressing the measurement button for confirmation.
semantic_fragments._source: 11 T1样机/PT9L-operation guide-20240828.via_lo_html.clean.md

semantic_fragments.content: Memory Mode: Press and hold the settings button for 3 seconds to enter the memory mode, and the memory icon 'M' will flash simultaneously. Release and use the settings button to toggle between the different memories, and latest memory will be shown as the first memory. If you want to view more memories of other modes, please choose your desired mode at first. Note: The thermometer turns off automatically after 15 seconds of inaction.
semantic_fragments._source: 11 T1样机/PT9L-operation guide-20240828.via_lo_html.clean.md

semantic_fragments.content: Memory Deletion Mode: In the power-off state, press and hold the measurement button and the settings button simultaneously for 8 seconds until the icon of 'dEL' and 'M' flash on screen. After 2 seconds, all memories will be deleted, and only the 'dEL' icon shows up on screen. And the thermometer will turn off automatically after 3 seconds.

semantic_fragments.content: Mute setting: Toggle the mute switch on the side of the thermometer to mute or unmute the device.

If battery capacity is low but adequate for measurements, the low power symbol will be displayed with the measurement results. However, if the battery capacity is too low for measurements, the screen will display a flashing low battery icon and automatically switch OFF after 15 seconds. To continue using the device, batteries must be replaced.

semantic_fragments.content: Replacing batteries instructions and safety warnings: (1) Press down the battery cover and slide the cover to open the battery compartment. (2) Remove the old batteries and install new batteries. (3) Refer to the battery polarity symbols to orient the batteries properly during installation. Make sure that the new batteries are tightly inserted into the battery compartment and the polarity is not reversed during installation. (4) Reinstall the battery cover to close the battery compartment. Safety notes: Comply with relevant state and local laws and regulations when disposing of the used batteries. For environmental safety, please do not discard batteries in the trash. Remove the batteries if the device will not be used more than one month. When using, shall not touch battery and the patient simultaneously. Do not throw batteries into fire. The typical service life of the new and unused batteries is approximately 1,000 measurements, and the service life may vary among different brands of batteries.

Dynamic measurement failed / target temperature outside range 89.6℉-109.2℉ (32℃-42.9℃) icons → Press and hold measurement button to restart dynamic measurement until result displayed; remove protective cap before measurement; follow User's Manual and repeat measurements. Environment temperature exceeds operational range 50℉-104℉ (10℃-40℃) or is unstable icon → Use thermometer within designed ambient temperature range. semantic_fragments.content: Temperature-taking hints: Body temperature varies from person to person and fluctuates during the day. It is suggested to know one's normal, healthy forehead temperature. Body temperature runs approximately from 95.9℉ to 99.5℉ (35.5℃–37.5℃). A rise over reference body temperature of 1℉ or more is generally an indication of fever. Different measurement sites give different readings; do not compare measurements taken from different sites.

semantic_fragments.content: Maintenance instructions: The thermometer is designed for home use. Between multiple users, clean the device using an alcohol swab or tissue moistened with 70% Isopropyl alcohol for more than 15 seconds; allow to dry for at least 5 minutes before use; repeat if not visually clean under magnification and adequate lighting. Cleaning steps validated per FDA Guidance 'Reprocessing Medical Devices in Health Care Settings: Validation Methods and Labeling'. The product is not waterproof — no liquid must enter the interior. Do not use abrasive cleaning agents, thinners, or benzene; never immerse in water or other cleaning liquids. Clean the probe gently with a cotton swab soaked in 70% Isopropyl. If probe/sensor is broken, contact customer services. iHealth Labs, Inc. has not authorized any agency or individual to carry out product repairs or maintenance. Do not disassemble or modify the thermometer. Do not place under direct sunlight, high temperature, or moist environments; avoid fire or harsh vibrations. Remove battery if device is not used for one month or more.
semantic_fragments._source: 11 T1样机/PT9L-operation guide-20240828.via_lo_html.clean.md

semantic_fragments.content: Disposal instructions: Dispose of batteries in accordance with local regulations. In EU countries, dispose of batteries at public collection points per 2012/19/EU WEEE Directive and REGULATION (EU) 2023/1542 Directive. Act according to local laws for disposal of used batteries. Remove batteries if the device will not be used for more than one month. Dispose of empty batteries at appropriate collection sites according to national or local regulations.

semantic_fragments.content: 术语和定义：3.1 红外体温计——通过使用红外传感器将测量到的温度显示出来的电子仪器。3.2 黑体模式——体温计显示从黑体处测量所得的温度的模式。3.3 恒温水槽——具有自动控温，提供恒定温度源的一种装置。此处使用的恒温水槽要求水温在工作区域内任意两点的温差不大于0.01℃，恒温时温度波动不大于0.015℃/15min。3.4 恒温水槽的稳定状态——恒温水槽到达预设的温度后，在15分钟内温度波动不超过0.015℃，则认为该恒温水槽达到稳定状态。3.5 黑体——能精确知道孔壁温度和在孔的任意开口处辐射率近似为1.0的孔状红外辐射基准源。

semantic_fragments.content: 测试条件要求：1) 工作电压 DC3.0V±0.1V；2) 测试标准黑体时，产品需在恒温房中放置120min以上；3) 恒温房温湿度要求：a）温度：23.0±2.0℃；b）相对湿度：50%RH±20%RH；c）大气压强：70~106kPa；4）恒温水槽精度要求：±0.02℃。
semantic_fragments._source: 11 T1样机/PT9L红外体温计产品检验标准 V1.0.doc.md

semantic_fragments.content: 常温精度测试：进入黑体模式方法为断电情况下按住按键后装入电池，显示"CAL"后松开按键。对被测水槽连续测量三次。精度要求：≥35℃且≤42℃为±0.2℃，其它为±0.3℃。对测试结果不符合规定的温度计，可复测两次，两次复测合格亦可作合格处理。
semantic_fragments._source: 11 T1样机/PT9L红外体温计产品检验标准 V1.0.doc.md

semantic_fragments.content: 低电压提示功能：3.0V供电时应能正常测量；低于2.7V时仍可进行测量但低电符号将随测量结果显示；低于2.5V时屏幕单独闪烁显示低电图标，15秒后将自动关机。
semantic_fragments._source: 11 T1样机/PT9L红外体温计产品检验标准 V1.0.doc.md

semantic_fragments.content: 背光灯测试：体温计应处于用户模式，不要进入黑体模式。测试34℃水槽时背光应为白色，测试35.7℃水槽时背光应为橙色，测试37℃水槽时背光应为红色。对测试结果不符合规定的温度计，可复测两次，两次复测合格亦可作合格处理。
semantic_fragments._source: 11 T1样机/PT9L红外体温计产品检验标准 V1.0.doc.md

semantic_fragments.content: 裸机跌落测试细则：跌落高度1M，跌3次，依次顺序底部、LCD面、有测量键面朝下方跌落各一次，探头部位不可跌落。应跌落于密度为700kg/M³、厚度为50mm的硬质木板或混凝土地面，若未完成跌落次数就已经解体或严重损伤时，应立即停止后续动作并分析。以产品自身重量自由下落，不可有外力加持，下落过程中产品不可在空中翻转，否则无效。
semantic_fragments._source: 11 T1样机/PT9L红外体温计产品检验标准 V1.0.doc.md

semantic_fragments.content: 产品寿命测试：产品整机寿命5年，假设平均每天使用5次，等效1万次使用寿命。对可影响整机寿命的电子元器件及结构组件进行测试。选取5个样品实际测量1万次，测试前后均按第8项进行测试，精度和功能均需正常，则认为产品寿命达到要求。
semantic_fragments._source: 11 T1样机/PT9L红外体温计产品检验标准 V1.0.doc.md

semantic_fragments.content: 电池寿命测试：要求测量次数≥1000次，待机能力≥6个月。模拟人体测试，通过测试不同状态的功耗推算出连续工作时间和待机时间，结果应满足设计要求。
semantic_fragments._source: 11 T1样机/PT9L红外体温计产品检验标准 V1.0.doc.md

semantic_fragments.content: 外观检验项目按面别（A面、B面、C面、D面、E面）分级管控，检验工具包括塞尺、目视、菲林卡。各面别缺陷判定标准如下：1.组装间隙：A/B/C面≤0.1mm，D/E面不影响组装及功能即可；2.段差：A/B/C面≤0.1mm，D/E面不影响组装及功能即可；3.脏污、指纹：A/B/C/D面不允许，E面不影响组装及功能即可；4.无感划伤/划痕线状缺陷：A面不允许，B面划伤不允许划痕L≤2mm W≤0.1mm N≤1，C面划伤不允许划痕L≤3mm W≤0.1mm N≤2 DS≥20mm，D面划伤L≤3mm W≤0.1mm划痕L≤10mm W≤0.3mm N≤2 DS≥20mm，E面不影响组装及功能即可；5.异色点/凹凸点：A面不允许，B面D≤0.20mm N≤1，C面D≤0.30mm N≤2 DS≥20mm，D面D≤0.30mm N≤2 DS忽略，E面不影响组装及功能即可；6.同色点：A面不允许，B面D≤0.30mm N≤1，C面D≤0.30mm N≤2 DS≥20mm，D面D≤0.40mm N≤2 DS忽略，E面不影响组装及功能即可；7.顶凸/顶白：A/B/C面不允许，D/E面不影响组装及功能即可；8.缩水、凹陷：A/B/C/D面不允许，E面不影响组装及功能即可；9.产品本体或装配后翘曲/变形：A/B面不允许，C/D面目测不明显/参照限度样本，E面不影响组装及功能即可。
semantic_fragments._source: 11 T1样机/PT9L红外体温计产品检验标准 V1.0.doc.md

semantic_fragments.content: 外观检验项目按面别（A/B/C/D/E面）分级管控，主要检验项目包括：注塑件拉伤、料口/水口、熔接线/气痕、毛边/批锋/分型线、高光面光泽度、缺料/断裂/裂痕/烧焦、金属部件锈蚀氧化、色差、螺丝、按键等。各缺陷根据面别严格程度不同，A面要求最严（多为不允许），E面要求最宽松（不影响组装及功能即可）。色差控制要求△E≤0.8，肉眼不可见。螺丝需紧固到位，无松动、未打紧现象，不允许漏装、滑丝/滑牙、划伤。按键需有正常回弹性。
semantic_fragments._source: 11 T1样机/PT9L红外体温计产品检验标准 V1.0.doc.md

semantic_fragments.content: 耐压测试：测试项1为电池正极到外壳，要求能承受DC1000V 1分钟内无绝缘击穿；测试项2为电池正极到探头，要求能承受DC1000V 1分钟内无绝缘击穿。具体操作详见IEC60601-1-2020/GB9706.1-2020相关条目。缺陷等级MA，每批抽3台，AC=0，RE=1，测试完的机器不可出货，作为留样保存。
semantic_fragments._source: 11 T1样机/PT9L红外体温计产品检验标准 V1.0.doc.md

semantic_fragments.content: 漏电流测试：测试项1为接触电流，要求正常状态≤0.1mA；测试项2为患者漏电流F型，要求正常状态≤5mA。具体操作详见IEC60601-1-2020/GB9706.1-2020相关条目。缺陷等级MA，每批抽3台，AC=0，RE=1，测试完的机器不可出货，作为留样保存。
semantic_fragments._source: 11 T1样机/PT9L红外体温计产品检验标准 V1.0.doc.md

semantic_fragments.content: 精度测试抽样方案参考GB2828.1-2012，缺陷等级为MA。其余功能检验项（上电自检、低电压提示、背光灯、测量单位切换、测量模式切换、提示音开关）均为MI缺陷等级，每批抽5个，AC=0，RE=1。电池反接和耐压测试缺陷等级为MA。
semantic_fragments._source: 11 T1样机/PT9L红外体温计产品检验标准 V1.0.doc.md

semantic_fragments.content: 彩盒检验具体要求：1）确认彩盒颜色与生产通知单是否相符合；2）确认彩盒印刷与生产通知单要求是否相符合；3）确认彩盒上所有条形码内容与生产通知单要求一致，字迹清楚不模糊，漏贴多贴或贴错不允许，标签位置方向贴错不允许，歪斜两水平位置相对差值≤1.5mm不允许盖住文字，表面无明显脏污破损开胶；4）彩盒粘合处不允许出现开胶现象，粘合边上下错位≤2mm，前后错位不允许露白，空隙不得影响正常成型；5）成型过程中彩盒插口插舌处不允许有瓦楞开胶现象；6）折线居中清晰，不得有破裂断线重线等现象；7）划痕30-50cm直视L≤10mm W≤0.3mm N≤1，未造成表面破损；8）脏污30-50cm直视无明显脏污；9）褶皱30-50cm直视，客户Logo和主图案L≤2mm，其他L≤5mm N≤1。

semantic_fragments.content: 外箱及配件检验具体要求：1）图案条码等内容大小图像与合同评审（样件）完全一致；2）外箱标签内容、材质及粘贴位置符合客户要求；3）标签粘贴不可盖住外箱文字，外箱破损造成字体条形码无法辨识不可以；4）撕裂长度≤2cm宽度≤5mm未在文字处允许有一个，穿透不可以，表面破损≤20cm²且不影响字符辨识允收一个，外箱标签破损长度>10mm不可以，倾斜超过30度不可以，标签褶皱N≤2；5）外箱没有被内箱或彩盒装入后顶起。

semantic_fragments.content: 该试验系统用新西兰兔来检测试验样品浸提液与试验系统直接接触引起的皮肤刺激反应，并类推到人类，但试验结果并不代表样品真正的皮肤刺激反应危险性。依据现行试验标准，新西兰大白兔被指定作为评价原发性皮肤刺激作用合适的动物模型。该试验采用20%的十二烷基硫酸钠作为皮肤刺激反应的阳性对照已经在苏州大学卫生与环境技术研究所试验得到证实。将试验样品浸提液0.5mL滴到2.5cm×2.5cm大小的吸收性纱布片，然后将纱布片直接与兔背部皮肤接触，被认为是最佳接触方式。

semantic_fragments.content: 试验步骤：试验前4-24小时将动物背部脊柱两侧被毛除去（约10cm×15cm），作为试验和观察部位。将试验样品浸提液和溶剂对照液各0.5mL分别滴到2.5cm×2.5cm大小的吸收性纱布片上备用。分别将浸透样品浸提液和溶剂对照液的纱布片直接接触兔脊柱两侧的皮肤，然后用绷带固定贴敷至少4小时。接触期结束后取下敷贴片。取下敷贴片后（1±0.1）h、（24±2）h、（48±2）h和（72±2）h观察敷贴部位及周围皮肤组织反应，包括红斑、水肿和坏死等记录之。

semantic_fragments.content: 试验步骤：试验前4-24小时将动物背部脊柱两侧被毛除去（约10 cm×15 cm），作为试验和观察部位。将试验样品浸提液和溶剂对照液各0.5 mL分别滴到2.5 cm×2.5 cm大小的吸收性纱布片上备用。分别将浸透样品浸提液和溶剂对照液的纱布片直接接触兔脊柱两侧的皮肤，然后用绷带固定贴敷至少4小时。接触期结束后取下敷贴片。取下敷贴片后（1±0.1）h、（24±2）h、（48±2）h和（72±2）h观察敷贴部位及周围皮肤组织反应，包括红斑、水肿和坏死等记录之。

semantic_fragments.content: 试验系统和给药途径确认：依据现行试验标准，新西兰大白兔被指定作为评价原发性皮肤刺激作用合适的动物模型。该试验采用20%的十二烷基硫酸钠作为皮肤刺激反应的阳性对照已经在苏州大学卫生与环境技术研究所试验得到证实（表3）。将试验样品浸提液0.5 mL滴到2.5 cm×2.5 cm大小的吸收性纱布片，然后将纱布片直接与兔背部皮肤接触，被认为是最佳接触方式。

semantic_fragments.content: 试验系统确认：小鼠成纤维细胞L929用来检测细胞毒性试验是因为其对试验样品浸提液反应灵敏。试验样品通过浸提液（用一种与试验系统相容的载体浸提）与试验系统接触，被认为是最佳给药途径，也是标准推荐的。
semantic_fragments._source: 11 T1样机/生物相容性/同PT5生物相容性报告/PT5-生物相容性-细胞毒性-SDWH-M201905262-1.pdf.md

semantic_fragments.content: 样品前处理：试验样品灭菌方式为辐照灭菌25 kGy Cobalt-60，对照样品与受试样品灭菌方式相同。样品浸提：无菌条件下取样，等数量取图中所有组件混合浸提。使用委托方提供的样品总表面积数据222.684 cm²，按3cm²:1mL浸提比例在密闭惰性容器内震荡浸提，浸提介质为含10%胎牛血清的MEM培养液。浸提前后浸提液状态未发生改变，pH值未经调整，未经过滤、离心、稀释等处理，阳性浸提液经过滤后使用。
semantic_fragments._source: 11 T1样机/生物相容性/同PT5生物相容性报告/PT5-生物相容性-细胞毒性-SDWH-M201905262-1.pdf.md

semantic_fragments.content: 试验步骤：1.将L929细胞培养在含10%胎牛血清和抗生素（青霉素100 U/mL，链霉素100μg/mL）的MEM培养液中，37°C，5% CO2培养箱中培养。用0.25%胰蛋白酶（含EDTA）消化细胞制备单细胞悬液，离心（200G，3min），调整细胞密度为1×10^5个/mL；2.接种细胞悬液到96孔培养板，每孔100μL，37°C培养箱（5% CO2，>90%湿度）培养24h；3.待细胞长成单层后，加入100μL不同浓度的试验样品浸提液（100%、75%、50%、25%）、空白对照液、阳性对照液（100%）和阴性对照液（100%），37°C，5% CO2培养24h，每组5个平行样；4.培养24h后进行细胞形态学观察，加50μL MTT（1mg/mL），37°C，5% CO2培养2h，吸弃上清，加100μL 99.9%纯度异丙醇溶解结晶；5.在酶标仪上以570nm为主吸收波长，650nm为参考波长测定吸光度值。

semantic_fragments.content: 质量检查要求：阴性对照无细胞毒性影响，阳性对照造成细胞毒性影响。未经处理的空白对照的OD570绝对值表明每孔接种的1×10^4个细胞以正常倍增时间成指数增长。空白对照的OD570平均值不能小于0.2。96孔板左侧（第2列）和右侧（第11列）作为空白对照（第1列和第12列不用作空白对照），左右两侧空白对照的平均值不能与所有空白的平均值相差超过15%。

semantic_fragments.content: 数据分析方法：使用SPSS 16.0计算各组测定的光密度值的均数±标准差（Mean±SD）。细胞活力（%）= 100 × [(OD570-OD650)样品组均值] / [(OD570-OD650)空白对照组均值]。50%浓度的样品浸提液与100%浓度的样品浸提液相比，细胞活力%应至少相同或更高，否则应重复试验。细胞活力%越低，表明受试样品潜在的细胞毒性越大。

semantic_fragments.content: 评价标准：50%的样品浸提液至少和100%的细胞活力相同或者比100%的细胞活力更高，否则应重复试验；细胞活力%越低，潜在的细胞毒性越大；细胞活力/空白组 < 70%，说明样品具有潜在的细胞毒性；100%试验样品浸提液的细胞活力%为最终结果。

【设计策划阶段2】根据设计输入汇总整理《软件需求规格书》；软件工程师拟制，软件主管审核，技术负责人批准；需包括存储器容量、信号输入/输出、功能、性能、人机接口、错误描述、响应时间、预期运行环境、阈值或特殊值、安全相关要求、软件测试规划等；接收准则：按评审计划评审并得到批准。
【设计开发阶段1】根据设计输入和需求规格书进行软件方案设计；输出《软件设计方案》；应包含运行环境、总体方案、设计规格、软硬件接口、降低风险措施；接收准则：按评审计划评审并得到批准。
【设计开发阶段2】根据设计输入、需求规格、设计方案输出软件流程图；输出《软件流程图》；接收准则：按评审计划评审并得到批准。
【设计开发阶段3】根据设计方案和流程图进行软件编码和调试；输出软件代码、目标代码、语音代码文件、EEPROM配置文件；接收准则：输出需要审核，测试通过后需要批准。
【验证测试阶段-计划】拟制《软件测试计划》；应包含测试阶段、人员职责、测试设备、测试说明、评价准则；接收准则：执行前应审核批准，测试记录应含通过结论并经审核签字。
【验证测试阶段1】对软件子程序进行测试；输出《子程序测试记录》；接收准则：按测试计划进行并得到批准。
【验证测试阶段2】进行系统测试；输出《软件测试报告》；接收准则：按测试计划进行并得到批准。
【设计更改】设计更改需求、方案评估并实施；评价设计更改后的风险控制及评价；输出相关设计更改记录及设计更改后风险控制措施验证及剩余风险评价报告；具体参见设计开发计划中"设计更改"部分要求。
【设计确认阶段1】拟制《用户现场测试计划》；应包含测试方法、测试要求、测试流程、接收准则；接收准则：应在设计确认活动前评审批准。
【设计确认阶段2】进行用户现场测试；输出用户现场测试报告；应包含用户自行实现预期用途方面、使用感受方面、测试异常情况、风险方面的总结；接收准则：测试报告应体现测试结果符合计划中的接收准则。
【维护】目标代码在生产过程中固化在产品内的MCU后无需软件维护。

semantic_fragments.content: 软件设计规格及实现方法：1.初始化功能：血压计上电后，初始化相关模块，等待移动设备与血压计建立蓝牙连接。2.关机功能：蓝牙无连接时，血压计自动关机，关机时，泵和阀都不能工作。3.加压过程：加压期间，袖带压力被显示在app界面中，当加压到190mmHg（机器无记忆时）或者高于上一次记忆的高压38mmHg时，泵会停止工作。4.加压出错检查功能：在加压过程中夹住气路，软件应该能检测出来，同时停止加压，打开阀，在app上显示错误信息；在加压过程中不连接袖带，几秒后软件应该能检测出气路断开，同时停止加压，在app上显示错误信息；在任何时候，袖带压力都不允许超过297mmHg超过1.5s。5.测量过程：每次检测到脉搏时，app界面上的心形符号会闪烁，同时袖带内压力及小波波形也显示在app界面上；在高压被检测到后，加压到合适的压力平台，机器会自动打开阀。6.计算过程：通过在测量过程中记录脉搏，来分别计算高压值、低压值、心率值。7.错误显示功能：机器主要检测的错误包括：检测不到零点、高低压未检出、压力大于297mmHg时间超过1.5s、袖带内的压力在15mmHg以上的时间超过160s、满度错误、数据传输失败、EEPROM访问失败、EEPROM三备份错误、电量低等。当血压计与移动设备建立连接时，应能将相关错误信息传输至移动设备。8.数据传输功能：在与移动设备蓝牙建立连接后，机器和移动设备间能够进行数据传输。

semantic_fragments.content: 降低风险的措施方案：1.袖带/腕带压力危害：软件每20ms循环监测袖带、腕带中的实时压力，判断当袖带、腕带压力大于297mmHg超过1.5s或压力大于15mmHg超过3分钟或压力大于300mmHg时，软件控制打开快速放气阀，迅速降低气压。2.显示信息不明确：软件对显示功能做测试，说明书解释显示的信息。3.不正确的算法：软件发布前进行临床算法验证。4.错误的数据转换：在数据传输过程中加入校验字节以确保数据传输的正确性。5.不正确的测试结果存储：在记忆的读操作中，采取两次比较读出的方式，当两次读出的数据均相同时，认为读出数据正确；在记忆的写操作中，采取写入后再读出校验的方式进行操作。

semantic_fragments.content: 软件系统将要实现的功能：1.初始化功能：血压计上电后，初始化相关模块，等待移动设备与血压计建立蓝牙连接；2.关机功能：蓝牙无连接时，血压计自动关机，关机时，泵和阀都不能工作；3.加压过程：加压期间，袖带压力被显示在app界面中，当加压到190mmHg（机器无记忆时）或者高于上一次记忆的高压38mmHg时，泵会停止工作；4.加压出错检查功能：在加压过程中夹住气路，软件应该能检测出来，同时停止加压，打开阀，在app上显示错误信息；在加压过程中不连接袖带，几秒后软件应该能检测出气路断开，同时停止加压，在app上显示错误信息；在任何时候，袖带压力都不允许超过297mmHg超过1.5s；5.测量过程：每次检测到脉搏时，app界面上的心形符号会闪烁，同时袖带内压力及小波波形也显示在app界面上；在高压被检测到后，加压到合适的压力平台，机器会自动打开阀；6.计算过程：通过在测量过程中记录脉搏，来分别计算高压值、低压值、心率值；7.错误显示功能：机器主要检测的错误包括：检测不到零点、高低压未检出、压力大于297mmHg时间超过1.5s、袖带内的压力在15mmHg以上的时间超过160s、满度错误、数据传输失败、EEPROM访问失败、EEPROM三备份错误、电量低等；8.数据传输功能：在与移动设备蓝牙建立连接后，机器和移动设备间能够进行数据传输。

semantic_fragments.content: 人机接口及软件与系统内部接口：键盘：1个按键，复位单片机。通讯接口：I2C总线，单片机为主设备，EEPROM为从设备；UART：单片机与蓝牙模块之间通讯；UART：单片机与测试工装通讯。人机交互描述：上电后系统进入关机态（低功耗状态），不开机并且不充电时灯不亮。在关机态，与手机蓝牙进行连接并建立通信后，绿灯常亮，启动iHealth APP点击开始测量键开始测量，测量过程中血压计将得到的压力及心跳信息传输至手机；测量完毕后，手机显示高压、低压、心率、血压分类、心律不齐（如果有）；测量过程中若出现异常，手机会显示相应提示信息。当电池电量不足时，手机会显示电量不足提示并且血压计上的红色LED灯闪烁。

semantic_fragments.content: 错误描述列表：Pressure system is unstable before measurement（搜索压力零点失败，压力不稳定达20秒）；Fail to detect systolic pressure（高压未检出或心跳小于4次）；Fail to detect diastolic pressure（低压未检出，或者高低压差为负值）；Pneumatic system blocked or cuff is too tight during inflation（气路阻塞、袖带太紧而加压过快）；Pneumatic system leakage or cuff is too loose during inflation（气路漏气、袖带过松而加压过慢）；Cuff pressure above 297mmHg（加压/测量中压力大于297mmHg的持续时间>1.5S）；More than 160 seconds with cuff pressure above 15 mmHg（一次测量中压力大于15mmHg的持续时间>160S）；EEPROM accessing error（EEPROM访问出错）；Three backups in EEPROM error（EEPROM中的3备份内容出错）；Span Error（机器SPAN值错误，SPAN<3000 or >6000）；Communication Error（通讯异常）；Low battery（低电压）。

semantic_fragments.content: PT9L红外体温计是一款快速测量体温的产品。具有简单易用、测量迅速、数据准确的特点。机芯主要由四部分组成：1、测温部分；2、电源部分；3、MCU系统；4、交互模块。测温部分利用温度传感器把人体温度转换成电信号，交给MCU进行处理。电源部分使用2颗AAA电池供电，使用升压芯片给整个系统提供电源，同时MCU的一路AD管脚接到电源上用于检测电压，当电压低于预设值时发出提示。MCU采用合泰公司的BH67F2762芯片，具有功能强大、性能稳定、抗干扰能力强、低功耗、价格低廉等优点，适于大规模生产。MCU的主要功能是采集温度传感器发出的电信号并计算出温度值，同时控制按键、显示和声音，使体温计完成测试及显示。交互模块由显示、声音和按键组成，负责接收用户的指令和给出温度信息；显示部分采用LCD屏幕由MCU直接驱动；声音部分采用蜂鸣器由MCU直接控制；按键部分同样由MCU控制接收用户的按键信息。

semantic_fragments.content: 主板贴片检测流程：上电后两个LED灯D1和D2全亮，屏幕显示CB1，然后显示软件版本号，2s后进入休眠，两个LED灯熄灭，显示黑屏，操作人员查看休眠电流，应小于50uA；按下按键B1唤醒，两个LED点亮，LCD全显，再次按下按键保存，CB1完成；若自检未通过，屏幕显示Er1。程序自动检测电池电压，外部NTC，红外传感器的贴片情况：电池电压在2.7V到3.3V之间；红外传感器测温应在10℃到40℃之间。否则，LCD会显示Er1错误提示，此时按下按键会循环显示上面两个测量结果供查找问题。

semantic_fragments.content: 斑马条（Zebra Strip / Elastomeric Connector）= 由导电硅胶（金/银粉填充）与绝缘硅胶交替条纹层叠而成的弹性连接器，专用于 LCD 段码屏与 PCBA 之间的无焊接电气连接。导电方向为垂直于长度方向（即沿厚度方向），电流从 LCD PIN 沿厚度方向传到 PCBA 焊盘，不沿长度方向短路。装配时被 LCD 与 PCBA 之间的弹性压缩力（推测 10-20% 压缩量）压紧，导电硅胶层与 LCD PIN + PCBA 焊盘做面接触。

semantic_fragments.content: CB2自检流程：上电后显示CB2，2s后进入休眠，检测休眠电流应大于1uA且小于20uA；按下测量按键唤醒，屏幕全显，白色背光开启，蜂鸣器响，检测工作电流应大于1mA且小于50mA；屏幕停止全显并出现静音符号时，拨动静音开关可切换静音/发音状态；按下测量按键，蜂鸣器响声停止，三色LED灯按照白橙红顺序点亮并循环，屏幕循环出现1、2、3数字；操作员观察三色LED灯无问题后按下设置按键保存；若自检未通过，屏幕显示Er2。

semantic_fragments.content: CB3常温标定流程：上电后显示CB3，1s后显示环温；按下按键后显示C30；按下按键采集C30，完成后显示C45；按下按键采集C45，完成后显示PAS，按键保存完成；注意采集C30后采集C45的时间间隔不能超过5s；标定失败显示Er3。环境条件要求：温度23.0±2.0℃，相对湿度50%RH±20%RH，大气压强70~106kPa，恒温水槽精度±0.02℃，初进入恒温房的机器需静置2小时。

semantic_fragments.content: CB4常温性能检查流程：上电后显示CB4，1s后显示环温，再过1s后显示C10；依次按键采集C10（完成显示C33）、C33（完成显示C37）、C37（完成显示C41）、C41（完成显示PAS）；任意步骤失败时显示实测温度0.5s，然后显示Er4。环境条件同CB3标定。

semantic_fragments.content: 主板贴片检测流程：上电后两个LED灯D1和D2全亮，屏幕显示CB1，然后显示软件版本号，2s后进入休眠，两个LED灯熄灭，显示黑屏，操作人员查看休眠电流，应小于30uA；按下按键S1唤醒，两个LED点亮，LCD全显；若自检全部通过，LCD显示"PAS"，按下按键S1保存，CB1完成；若自检未通过，屏幕显示Er1。程序自动检测电池电压、外部NTC、红外传感器的贴片情况：电池电压在2.7V到3.3V之间；外部NTC温度在23℃到27℃之间（此处为10K的标准电阻）；红外传感器测温应在10℃到40℃之间。否则LCD会显示ER1错误提示，此时按下按键会循环显示上面三个测量结果供查找问题。

semantic_fragments.content: Device description: The iHealth PT9L Infrared No-Touch Forehead Thermometer is hand-held, reusable, battery operated device, which can measure human body temperature on the skin temperature on one's forehead. Its operation is based on measuring the natural thermal radiation from the central forehead. Put the probe of the thermometer is onto the skin of a patient's central forehead. Pressing the activation button to start the measurement of proposed infrared radiation. The electrical signal read out from the detector is fed to the circuit for amplification and calculation. The final measured temperature will be appeared on a LCD display.

semantic_fragments.content: Test method: Step1: Sequence the Participants and sign Serial numbers. Step2: Verify reference thermometer accuracy using water bath. Step3: Supervisor takes DUT and prepares measurement. Step4: Perform three consecutive measurements with time interval no more than 1 min, record results. Step5: Take one RCT oral temperature measurement, record results. Step6: Repeat for all participants (odd-numbered: DUT first then RCT; even-numbered: RCT first then DUT). Final step: Verify reference thermometer accuracy again with water bath.

semantic_fragments.content: This document is a Checklist of EN 62366-1:2015+A1:2020 (Medical electrical equipment – Application of usability engineering to medical devices) for the PT9L Infrared Forehead Thermometer. It covers the general requirements under Clause 4 including usability engineering process establishment, risk control as it relates to user interface design, and information for safety as it relates to usability.
semantic_fragments._source: 18 设计确认/PT9L Checklist of IEC 62366-1 2021.pdf.md

semantic_fragments.content: When, in accordance with the priorities of 4.1.2, information for SAFETY is used as a RISK CONTROL measure, the MANUFACTURER shall subject this information to the USABILITY ENGINEERING PROCESS to determine that the information is perceivable by, understandable to, and supports CORRECT USE of the MEDICAL DEVICE by USERS of the intended USER PROFILES in the context of the intended USE ENVIRONMENT. Conscious disregard of such information for SAFETY by the USER is considered to be an intentional act or intentional omission of an act that is counter to or violates NORMAL USE and is also beyond any further reasonable means of USER INTERFACE-related RISK CONTROL by the MANUFACTURER (i.e. ABNORMAL USE).
semantic_fragments._source: 18 设计确认/PT9L Checklist of IEC 62366-1 2021.pdf.md

semantic_fragments.content: The level of effort and the choice of methods and tools used to perform the USABILITY ENGINEERING PROCESS may vary based on: a) the size and COMPLEXITY of the USER INTERFACE; b) the SEVERITY of the HARM associated with the use of the MEDICAL DEVICE; c) the extent or complexity of the USE SPECIFICATION; d) the presence of USER INTERFACE OF UNKNOWN PROVENANCE; and e) the extent of the modification to an existing MEDICAL DEVICE USER INTERFACE that had been subjected to the USABILITY ENGINEERING PROCESS.
semantic_fragments._source: 18 设计确认/PT9L Checklist of IEC 62366-1 2021.pdf.md

semantic_fragments.content: During the identification of HAZARDS and HAZARDOUS SITUATIONS (clause 5.3), the following shall be considered: USE SPECIFICATION including USER PROFILE(S) (see 5.1); information on HAZARDS and HAZARDOUS SITUATIONS known for existing USER INTERFACES of MEDICAL DEVICES of a similar type, if available; and identified USE ERRORS (see 5.2).
semantic_fragments._source: 18 设计确认/PT9L Checklist of IEC 62366-1 2021.pdf.md

semantic_fragments.content: Clause 5.4 requires the MANUFACTURER to identify and describe the reasonably foreseeable HAZARD-RELATED USE SCENARIOS associated with the identified HAZARDS and HAZARDOUS SITUATIONS. The description of each identified HAZARD-RELATED USE SCENARIO shall include all TASKS and their sequences as well as the SEVERITY of the associated HARM. The results of this identification shall be stored in the USABILITY ENGINEERING FILE.
semantic_fragments._source: 18 设计确认/PT9L Checklist of IEC 62366-1 2021.pdf.md

semantic_fragments.content: Clause 5.5 requires the MANUFACTURER to select the HAZARD-RELATED USE SCENARIOS to be included in the SUMMATIVE EVALUATION. Selection options include: all HAZARD-RELATED USE SCENARIOS; a subset based on SEVERITY of potential HARM that could be caused by USE ERROR (e.g. for which medical intervention would be needed); or a subset based on SEVERITY of potential HARM and other circumstances specific to the MEDICAL DEVICE and the MANUFACTURER. A summary of any selection scheme, the rationale for its use and the results of applying it shall be stored in the USABILITY ENGINEERING FILE.
semantic_fragments._source: 18 设计确认/PT9L Checklist of IEC 62366-1 2021.pdf.md

semantic_fragments.content: Clause 5.6 requires the MANUFACTURER to establish and maintain a USER INTERFACE SPECIFICATION. The specification shall consider: the USE SPECIFICATION (see 5.1); the known or foreseeable USE ERRORS associated with the MEDICAL DEVICE (see 5.2); and the HAZARD-RELATED USE SCENARIOS (see 5.4). The USER INTERFACE SPECIFICATION shall include: testable technical requirements relevant to the USER INTERFACE, including requirements for parts associated with selected RISK CONTROL measures; an indication as to whether ACCOMPANYING DOCUMENTATION is required; and an indication as to whether MEDICAL DEVICE-specific training is required. The USER INTERFACE SPECIFICATION shall be stored in the USABILITY ENGINEERING FILE and may be integrated into other specifications.
semantic_fragments._source: 18 设计确认/PT9L Checklist of IEC 62366-1 2021.pdf.md

semantic_fragments.content: Clause 5.7.1 specifies that the USER INTERFACE EVALUATION plan shall: a) document the objective and identify the method of any planned FORMATIVE EVALUATIONS and SUMMATIVE EVALUATIONS; b) if USABILITY TESTS are employed, document which USER GROUPS are intended to be included in the test, document the test environment and other conditions of use based on the USE SPECIFICATION, specify whether ACCOMPANYING DOCUMENTATION is provided during the test, and specify whether MEDICAL DEVICE-specific training is provided prior to the test and the minimum elapsed time between training and the beginning of the test. USER INTERFACE EVALUATION methods may be quantitative or qualitative and may be performed in a laboratory setting, simulated USE ENVIRONMENT or actual USE ENVIRONMENT. The plan may be integrated into other plans and shall be stored in the USABILITY ENGINEERING FILE.
semantic_fragments._source: 18 设计确认/PT9L Checklist of IEC 62366-1 2021.pdf.md

semantic_fragments.content: 5.7.3 SUMMATIVE EVALUATION planning: For each selected HAZARD-RELATED USE SCENARIO, the USER INTERFACE EVALUATION plan for SUMMATIVE EVALUATION shall specify: a) the evaluation method being used and a rationale that the method produces OBJECTIVE EVIDENCE; b) which part of the USER INTERFACE is being evaluated; c) where applicable, the criteria for determining whether the information for SAFETY is perceivable, understandable and supports CORRECT USE of the MEDICAL DEVICE (4.1.3); d) the availability of the ACCOMPANYING DOCUMENTATION and provision of training during the SUMMATIVE EVALUATION; and e) for a USABILITY TEST: how the characteristics of the test participants are representative of the intended PROFILES; justifying how the test participants are grouped into distinct USER GROUPS for the purpose of determining the number of test participants; the test environment and conditions of use and a rationale for how they are adequately representative of the intended USE ENVIRONMENT; the definition of CORRECT USE for each HAZARD-RELATED USE SCENARIO; and the method of collecting data during the USABILITY TEST for the subsequent analysis of observed USE ERRORS and use difficulties. The SUMMATIVE EVALUATION may be performed in a single evaluation or multiple evaluations.
semantic_fragments._source: 18 设计确认/PT9L Checklist of IEC 62366-1 2021.pdf.md

semantic_fragments.content: 5.8 Perform USER INTERFACE design, implementation and FORMATIVE EVALUATION: The MANUFACTURER shall design and implement the USER INTERFACE, including the ACCOMPANYING DOCUMENTATION if needed, and training capability, if needed, as described in the USER INTERFACE SPECIFICATION. The MANUFACTURER shall utilize, as appropriate, USABILITY ENGINEERING methods and techniques, including FORMATIVE EVALUATION to accomplish this design and implementation. The results of the utilized FORMATIVE EVALUATION shall be stored in the USABILITY ENGINEERING FILE. Where new USE ERRORS, HAZARDS, HAZARDOUS SITUATIONS or HAZARD-RELATED USE SCENARIOS are discovered during this step, the MANUFACTURER shall repeat the steps of Clause 5 as appropriate. If training on the specific MEDICAL DEVICE is required for the safe use of the MEDICAL DEVICE by the intended USER, the MANUFACTURER shall design and implement a training capability for the EXPECTED SERVICE LIFE of the MEDICAL DEVICE by doing at least one of the following: provide the materials necessary for training; ensure that the materials necessary for training are available; make the training available; or make training available to the RESPONSIBLE ORGANIZATION that enables it to train its USERS.
semantic_fragments._source: 18 设计确认/PT9L Checklist of IEC 62366-1 2021.pdf.md

semantic_fragments.content: 5.9 Perform SUMMATIVE EVALUATION of the USABILITY of the USER INTERFACE: Upon completion of the design and implementation of the USER INTERFACE, the MANUFACTURER shall perform a SUMMATIVE EVALUATION of each HAZARD-RELATED USE SCENARIO selected in 5.5 on the final or production equivalent USER INTERFACE according to the USER INTERFACE EVALUATION plan. For SUMMATIVE EVALUATION, the MANUFACTURER may use data obtained from the SUMMATIVE EVALUATIONS of products with an equivalent USER INTERFACE together with a technical rationale for how this data is applicable. The results shall be stored in the USABILITY ENGINEERING FILE. The MANUFACTURER shall analyse the data of the SUMMATIVE EVALUATION and shall identify all USE ERRORS and use difficulties that occurred. If a USE ERROR or use difficulty can lead to a HAZARDOUS SITUATION, the root cause of any such USE ERROR or use difficulty shall be determined. The root causes should be determined based on methods including observations of USER performance as well as subjective comments from the USER.
semantic_fragments._source: 18 设计确认/PT9L Checklist of IEC 62366-1 2021.pdf.md

semantic_fragments.content: If new USE ERRORS, HAZARDS, HAZARDOUS SITUATIONS or HAZARD-RELATED USE SCENARIOS are discovered during data analysis: if yes, then the MANUFACTURER shall repeat the activities of Clause 5 as appropriate; if not, the MANUFACTURER shall determine whether further improvement of the USER INTERFACE design as it relates to SAFETY is necessary and practicable. 1) if yes, then the MANUFACTURER shall re-enter the USABILITY ENGINEERING PROCESS at 5.6; 2) if not, then the MANUFACTURER shall: i) document why improvement is not necessary or not practicable; ii) identify the data from the USABILITY ENGINEERING PROCESS needed to determine the RESIDUAL RISK related to use; and iii) evaluate RESIDUAL RISK according to ISO 14971:2019, 7.3.
semantic_fragments._source: 18 设计确认/PT9L Checklist of IEC 62366-1 2021.pdf.md

semantic_fragments.content: Annex C - Evaluation of a USER INTERFACE OF UNKNOWN PROVENANCE (UOUP): C.2.4 states that if the MANUFACTURER determines that changes to any part of the USER INTERFACE are required to reduce RISK to an acceptable level, those changes shall not be considered UOUP and shall be subject to the requirements of 5.1 through 5.9.
semantic_fragments._source: 18 设计确认/PT9L Checklist of IEC 62366-1 2021.pdf.md

semantic_fragments.content: Table 5.7 可用性工程文件结果表：用户界面评估计划。制造商须建立并维护 USER INTERFACE EVALUATION 计划，内容包括：FORMATIVE 和 SUMMATIVE 评估的目标与方法；可用性测试中的用户群体、测试环境及使用条件、随附文件提供情况、培训提供情况及培训与测试间最短间隔时间。FORMATIVE EVALUATION 计划须说明评估方法、被评估的用户界面部分及执行时间节点。SUMMATIVE EVALUATION 计划须针对每个已选 HAZARD-RELATED USE SCENARIO 进行规定（内容在本片段末尾截断，未完整呈现）。对应文件为 Usability Engineering File CE-PT9L-12，相关章节为第 7、7.1、7.2 节。

semantic_fragments.content: Section 5.2 - The MANUFACTURER shall identify USER INTERFACE characteristics that could be related to SAFETY as part of a RISK ANALYSIS performed according to ISO 14971:2019, 5.3. This identification may also be performed using the tools and techniques from the USABILITY ENGINEERING PROCESS. This identification shall include consideration of the PRIMARY OPERATING FUNCTIONS that are provided in applicable particular MEDICAL DEVICE SAFETY standards. Based on the identified USER INTERFACE characteristics and USE SPECIFICATION, the MANUFACTURER shall identify the USE ERRORS that could occur and are related to the USER INTERFACE. This identification may be accomplished by conducting a TASK analysis. The results of this identification of characteristics related to SAFETY and potential USE ERRORS shall be stored in the USABILITY ENGINEERING FILE.

semantic_fragments.content: Section 5.3 - The MANUFACTURER shall identify known or foreseeable HAZARDS and HAZARDOUS SITUATIONS, which could affect PATIENTS, USERS or others, related to use of the MEDICAL DEVICE. This identification shall be conducted as part of a RISK ANALYSIS performed according to ISO 14971:2019, 5.4. During the identification, the following shall be considered: USE SPECIFICATION including USER PROFILE(S); information on HAZARDS and HAZARDOUS SITUATIONS known for existing USER INTERFACES of MEDICAL DEVICES of a similar type (N/A); and identified USE ERRORS. Results shall be stored in the USABILITY ENGINEERING FILE.

semantic_fragments.content: Section 5.1 - The MANUFACTURER shall prepare a USE SPECIFICATION. The USE SPECIFICATION shall include: intended medical indication; intended PATIENT population; intended part of the body or type of tissue applied to or interacted with; intended USER PROFILE; USE ENVIRONMENT; and operating principle. All elements are described in section 2.1 of Usability Engineering File (document no. CE-PT9L-12).

semantic_fragments.content: The USER INTERFACE SPECIFICATION shall consider: the USE SPECIFICATION (see 5.1); the known or foreseeable USE ERRORS associated with the MEDICAL DEVICE (see 5.2); and the HAZARD-RELATED USE SCENARIOS (see 5.4). The USER INTERFACE SPECIFICATION shall include: testable technical requirements relevant to the USER INTERFACE, including the requirements for those parts of the USER INTERFACE associated with the selected RISK CONTROL measures; an indication as to whether ACCOMPANYING DOCUMENTATION is required; and an indication as to whether MEDICAL DEVICE-specific training is required. The USER INTERFACE SPECIFICATION shall be stored in the USABILITY ENGINEERING FILE. The USER INTERFACE SPECIFICATION may be integrated into other specifications. semantic_fragments.content: The MANUFACTURER shall establish and maintain a USER INTERFACE EVALUATION plan for the USER INTERFACE SPECIFICATION (section 5.7, 5.7.1). The USER INTERFACE EVALUATION plan shall: 1. document the objective and identify the method of any planned FORMATIVE EVALUATIONS and SUMMATIVE EVALUATIONS; 2. if USABILITY TESTS are employed, document which USER GROUPS are intended to be included in the test; document the test environment and other conditions of use, based on the USE SPECIFICATION; specify whether ACCOMPANYING DOCUMENTATION is provided during the test; and specify whether MEDICAL DEVICE-specific training is provided prior to the test and the minimum elapsed time between the training and the beginning of the test. USER INTERFACE EVALUATION methods may be quantitative or qualitative. USER INTERFACE EVALUATION may be performed in a variety of locations, such as in a laboratory setting, in a simulated USE ENVIRONMENT or in the actual USE ENVIRONMENT. The USER INTERFACE EVALUATION plan may be integrated into other plans. The USER INTERFACE EVALUATION plan shall be stored in the USABILITY ENGINEERING FILE. See section 7 of Usability Engineering File (document no. CE-PT9L-12).

semantic_fragments.content: SUMMATIVE EVALUATION planning (5.7.3): For each selected HAZARD-RELATED USE SCENARIO (see 5.5), the USER INTERFACE EVALUATION plan for SUMMATIVE EVALUATION shall specify: 1. the evaluation method being used and a rationale that the method produces OBJECTIVE EVIDENCE; 2. which part of the USER INTERFACE is being evaluated; 3. where applicable, the criteria for determining whether the information for SAFETY is perceivable, understandable and supports CORRECT USE of the MEDICAL DEVICE (4.1.3); 4. the availability of the ACCOMPANYING DOCUMENTATION and provision of training during the SUMMATIVE EVALUATION; and 5. for a USABILITY TEST: how the characteristics of the test participants are representative of the intended PROFILES; justifying how the test participants are grouped into distinct USER GROUPS for the purpose of determining the number of test participants; the test environment and conditions of use and a rationale for how they are adequately representative of the intended USE ENVIRONMENT; the definition of CORRECT USE for each HAZARD-RELATED USE SCENARIO; and the method of collecting data during the USABILITY TEST for the subsequent analysis of observed USE ERRORS and use difficulties. semantic_fragments.content: The MANUFACTURER shall analyse the data of the SUMMATIVE EVALUATION and shall identify all USE ERRORS and use difficulties that occurred. If new USE ERRORS, HAZARDS, HAZARDOUS SITUATIONS or HAZARD-RELATED USE SCENARIOS are discovered during this data analysis: if yes, then the MANUFACTURER shall repeat the activities of Clause 5 as appropriate; if not, the MANUFACTURER shall determine whether further improvement of the USER INTERFACE design as it relates to SAFETY is necessary and practicable. 1) if yes, then the MANUFACTURER shall re-enter the USABILITY ENGINEERING PROCESS at 5.6; 2) if not, then the MANUFACTURER shall: 1. document why improvement is not necessary or not practicable; 2. identify the data from the USABILITY ENGINEERING PROCESS needed to determine the RESIDUAL RISK related to use; and 3. semantic_fragments.content: The purpose of Usability Engineering, also known as Human Factors Engineering, for the Infrared Forehead Thermometer is to provide a systematic process to analyze, specify, develop, and evaluate the usability of the device in relation to safety. This process aims to assess and mitigate risks associated with normal use. By considering the specific needs and abilities of users, Usability Engineering enhances the usability, safety, and user experience of the Infrared Forehead Thermometer, reducing the likelihood of errors and optimizing the overall effectiveness.

(3) Ensure adequate budget allocation for usability engineering activities during project planning cycles. (4) Develop a customized usability engineering project plan for each product development effort; define activity timelines, team roles, and responsibilities tailored to the project; integrate usability engineering into the overall medical device project plan; address the need to reduce use error risks and create satisfying medical devices.

5.3 Establish user interface specification: The user interface specification for the Infrared Forehead Thermometer is as follows:
a. Visual Design and Layout: The device and the display should be easily readable, button should be easily understandable, user can complete the measurement with only the device and instruction for use.
b. Feedback and Indicators: Provide clear visual feedback to confirm device operation, mode, and settings. Indicate battery status.
c. Safety Features: Incorporate features to prevent accidental changes in settings during use. Implement user lock-out mechanisms to avoid unintended modifications.
d. Usability Testing: Conduct usability testing with representative users according to EN 62366-1 standard to validate the effectiveness and ease of use. Identify potential use errors and areas for improvement based on user feedback.

Tailoring the usability engineering effort for a Infrared Forehead Thermometer is essential to address the specific risks and complexities associated with its use. The level of effort required for usability engineering can vary significantly depending on the nature of the device, its functions, and potential risks. Several considerations should guide the tailoring process:

**Risk Assessment and Severity:** Begin by assessing the potential risks associated with the Infrared Forehead Thermometer's usability. Focus on identifying hazards and their potential causes that could lead to harm. Consider the severity of potential harm when determining the scope of usability engineering efforts. High-severity risks should receive greater attention.

**Device Complexity:** Consider the complexity of the Infrared Forehead Thermometer's functions and user interactions. Devices with more intricate operations may require more extensive usability engineering efforts. The complexity could range from simple devices like lancing devices to more complex ones like haemodialysis equipment.

**Novelty:** For novel devices lacking post-production data, prioritize the severity of potential harm over estimating occurrence probability. This approach helps tailor usability engineering efforts to address worst-case scenarios and focuses on minimizing harm.

**Modification and Change:** When modifying an existing user interface, focus on the changed elements and their effects on device use. If unchanged elements remain unaffected, additional usability engineering effort might not be needed. Changes that do not impact the user interface or use specifications might not necessitate additional effort.

**Previous Records:** If previous usability engineering records are available for an existing user interface, leverage these records to streamline the usability engineering effort. Tailor activities based on the changes made to the user interface and the relevance of previous records.

**User Research and Testing:** Tailor the extent of user research and testing based on device complexity and risks. Research efforts might involve a smaller or larger number of participants. The usability testing scope could vary from involving a comprehensive set of users to specific user groups with distinct responsibilities.

**Summative Evaluation:** Tailor the quantity and complexity of summative evaluations based on the risk assessment. For some cases, a single usability test with a single user group might suffice to assess hazard-related use scenarios. In other instances, multiple sessions with different user groups might be necessary to assess various scenarios.

**Iterative Process:** Good usability engineering practice involves iterative evaluations. If initial summative evaluations indicate modifications are needed, focus subsequent evaluations on those specific elements of the user interface affected by the changes.

**Usability Engineering Plan:** Develop a tailored usability engineering plan that outlines the specific activities, participants, and methods for each phase of usability engineering. This plan ensures that efforts are aligned with the device's characteristics and risks.

By tailoring the usability engineering effort to the unique characteristics of the Infrared Forehead Thermometer, you can effectively identify, mitigate, and control usability-related risks, ensuring the safety and effectiveness of the device's user interface.

semantic_fragments.content: 申报产品PT9L基本原理：本产品使用红外传感器，在不接触额头的情况下，可接收额头温度所辐射出的红外线信号，并转换成感应电压，通过测量该感应电压，并经过计算处理修正后，将测量温度以数字的形式通过LCD显示器显示出测量体温值，同时喇叭响起，测量过程结束。同品种PT3基本原理相同，但显示器为LED显示器，提示方式为机身振动。

13. 禁忌症：申报产品明确前额有局部病变（炎症、创伤、近期手术等）不建议使用，描述更加全面

semantic_fragments.content: The iHealth PT9L Infrared No-Touch Forehead Thermometer is hand-held, reusable, battery operated device, which can measure human body temperature on the skin temperature on one's forehead. Its operation is based on measuring the natural thermal radiation from the central forehead. Put the probe of the thermometer is onto the skin of a patient's central forehead. Pressing the activation button to start the measurement of proposed infrared radiation. The electrical signal read out from the detector is fed to the circuit for amplification and calculation. The final measured temperature will be appeared on a LCD display.

semantic_fragments.content: Test method: Step 1: Sequence the Participants and sign Serial numbers for them according to participant time. Step 2: Using a water bath to verify the laboratory accuracy of the reference thermometer. Step 3: The supervisor takes the DUT, prepares to take measurement for the first subject. Step 4: Perform three consecutive measurement procedures with the time interval no more than 1 min between each reading. And record the test results. Step 5: Take one measurement with the RCT to get oral temperature, and record the test results. Step 6: Take one measurement with the Braun thermometer to get forehead temperature, and record the test results. Step 7: Repeat steps 3 to 6 to complete all the measurements of the participants. Note: participants signed with odd numbers were measured with DUT first and then with RCT and Braun thermometer; participants signed with even numbers were measured with RCT and Braun thermometer first and then with DUT. Step 8: Using a water bath to verify the laboratory accuracy of the reference thermometer again.

semantic_fragments.content: 所有高于绝对零温度的物体都会根据其温度发射一定百分比的红外辐射能量。辐射能量的多少与波长的分布有着非常密切的关系。当人的额头温度在36-37℃时，会发出波长9-13μm的红外辐射。基于此原理，利用该产品前端的红外热传感器通过测量前额至颞动脉上方热辐射来准确快速显示人的体温。

semantic_fragments.content: Mode 1 – Battery power Standby mode: Install battery to the EUT and keep the EUT in standby state. Mode 2 – Battery power Test mode: PT9L is powered by the internal battery. Hold down the power button to install the battery and set PT9L in UE1 mode. During the radiation disturbance test, PT9L detects the air and carries out continuous measurement. During the immunity test, the temperature sensor detection is point to the blackbody, and the blackbody is set to 37°C. The temperature is continuously measured and compared with the blackbody temperature. The measurement accuracy is ±0.2°C.

semantic_fragments.content: Radiated emission test procedure: Before final measurements, a pre-scan was performed in the spectrum mode with the peak detector to find out the maximum emission spectrum signature data plots of the EUT. The frequencies of maximum emission were determined in the final radiated emissions measurement; the physical arrangement of the test system and associated cabling was varied in order to determine the effect on the EUT's emissions in amplitude, direction and frequency. At each frequency, the EUT was rotated 360°, and the Antenna was raised and lowered from 1 to 4 meters in order to determine the maximum disturbance. Measurements were performed for both horizontal and vertical Antenna polarization.

semantic_fragments.content: ESD Test Setup Procedure: (1) Contact discharge was applied only to conductive surfaces of the EUT. Air discharge was applied only to non-conducted surfaces of the EUT. (2) The EUT was put on a 0.8m high wooden table for table-top equipment or 0.1m high for floor standing equipment standing on the ground reference plane (GRP). (3) A horizontal coupling plane (HCP) 1.6m by 0.8m in size was placed on the table, and the EUT with its cables were isolated from the HCP by an insulating support thicker than 0.5mm. The VCP 0.5m by 0.5m in size while HCP were constructed from the same material type and thickness as that of the GRP, and connected to the GRP via a 470kΩ resistor at each end. The distance between EUT and any of the other metallic surfaces except the GRP, HCP and VCP was greater than 1m. (4) During the contact discharges, the tip of the discharge electrode touched the EUT before the discharge switch is operated. During the air discharges, the round discharge tip was approached as fast as possible to touch the EUT. (5) After each discharge, the ESD generator was removed from the EUT, the generator is then retriggered for a new single discharge. For ungrounded product, a discharge cable with two resistances was used after each discharge to remove remnant electrostatic voltage. 10 times of each polarity single discharge were applied to HCP and VCP.

semantic_fragments.content: Radiated Immunity Test Setup and Procedure: 1. For table-top equipment, the EUT was placed in the chamber on a non-conductive table 0.8m high. For floor-standing equipment, the EUT was mounted on a non-conductive support 0.1m above the supporting plane. 2. If possible, a minimum of 1m of cable is exposed to the electromagnetic field. Excess length of cables interconnecting units of the EUT shall be bundled low-inductively in the approximate center of the cable to form a bundle 30 cm to 40 cm in length. 3. The EUT was initially placed with one face coincident with the calibration plane. The EUT face being illuminated was contained within the UFA (Uniform Field Area). 4. The frequency ranges to be considered were swept with the signal modulated and pausing to adjust the RF signal level or to switch oscillators and Antennas as necessary. The frequency range was swept incrementally, the step size was not exceed 1% of the preceding frequency value. 5. The dwell time of the amplitude modulated carrier at each frequency was not be less than the time necessary for the EUT to be exercised and to respond, and was not less than 0.5 s. 6. The test normally was performed with the generating Antenna facing each side of the EUT. 7. The polarization of the field generated by each Antenna necessitates testing each selected side twice, once with the Antenna positioned vertically and again with the Antenna positioned horizontally. 8. The EUT was performed in a configuration to actual installation conditions, a video camera and/or an audio monitor were used to monitor the performance of the EUT.

semantic_fragments.content: EFT Test Setup (6.5.1): The EUT was placed on a ground reference plane (GRP) insulated by an insulating support 0.1m thick and the GRP was placed on a 0.8m high wooden table for table-top equipment. For floor standing equipment, the EUT was placed on a 0.1m high wooden support above the GRP. The GRP shall project beyond the EUT and the clamp by at least 0.1m on all sides. The distance between the EUT and any other metallic surface except the GRP was greater than 0.5m. All cables to the EUT was placed on the insulation support 0.1m above GRP. Cables not subject to EFT was routed as far as possible from cable under test to minimize coupling between cables. The length of signal and power cable between the EUT and EFT generator was 0.5m. If the cable is a non-detachable supply cable more than 0.5m, the excess length shall be folded to avoid a flat coil and situated at a distance of 0.1m above the GRP. The EUT was conducted the below specified level voltage test for line to neutral or line to neutral to earth (for clamp coupling is for the signal line), 120 seconds duration. If the equipment contains identical ports, only one was tested; multiconductor cables were tested as a single cable. Interface ports intended by the manufacturer to be connected to data cables not longer than 3m did not be tested. During the test, the EUT was tested with the hand-held parts terminated with artificial hand.

semantic_fragments.content: Surge Test Setup (6.6.1): The EUT was placed on a ground reference plane (GRP) insulated by an insulating support 0.1m thick and the GRP was placed on a 0.8m high wooden table for table-top equipment. For floor standing equipment, the EUT was placed on a 0.1m high wooden support above the GRP. The 1.2/50 µs surge was to be applied to the EUT power supply terminals via the capacitive coupling network. Decoupling networks were required in order to avoid possible adverse effects on equipment not under test that may be powered by the same lines and to provide sufficient decoupling impedance to the surge wave. The power cord between the EUT and the coupling/decoupling network shall not exceed 2m in length. The EUT was conducted 1kV test voltage for line to line and line to neutral, and 2kV test voltage for line to earth and neutral to earth, five positive pulses and five negative pulses each at 90° and 270° for AC power ports and five positive pulses and five negative surge pulses for DC power ports. The test levels were applied with a 2Ω generator source impedance for power supply terminals and 40Ω output impedance for interconnection lines. Tests were done at repetition rate 1 per minute.

semantic_fragments.content: Test Setup and Procedure for Conducted RF Immunity (6.7.1): The EUT was placed on an insulating support of 0.1m height above a ground reference plane, arranged and connected to satisfy its functional requirement. All cables exiting the EUT was supported at a height of at least 30 mm above the ground reference plane. The coupling and decoupling devices were required, they were located between 0.1m and 0.3m from the EUT. Each AE, used with clamp injection, shall be placed on an insulating support 0.1m above the ground reference plane. A decoupling network shall be installed on each cable between the EUT and AE except the cable under test. The frequency range was swept from 150 kHz to 80 MHz, using the signal levels established during the setting process, and with the disturbance signal 80% amplitude modulated with a 1kHz sine wave. Where the frequency was swept incrementally, the step size do not exceed 1% of the preceding frequency value. The dwell time at each frequency was not less than 0.5 s. During the test, the EUT was tested with the hand-held parts terminated with artificial hand.

semantic_fragments.content: Test Setup and Procedure for Voltage Dips and Interruptions (6.8.1): The EUT was placed on a ground reference plane (GRP) insulated by an insulating support 0.1m thick and the GRP was placed on a 0.8m high wooden table for table-top equipment. For floor standing equipment, the EUT was placed on a 0.1m high wooden support above the GRP. The test was performed with the EUT connected to the test generator with the shortest power supply cable as specified by the EUT manufacturer. The EUT was tested for each selected combination of test level and duration with a sequence of three dips/interruptions with intervals of 10 s minimum. Each representative mode of operation was tested. For EUT with more than one power cord, each power cord was tested individually.

semantic_fragments.content: The EUT was placed on a ground reference plane (GRP) insulated by an insulating support 0.1m thick and the GRP was placed on a 0.8m high wooden table for table-top equipment. For floor standing equipment, the EUT was placed on a 0.1m high wooden support above the GRP. The EUT was configured and connected to satisfy its functional requirements. The power supply, input and output circuits was connected to the sources of power supply, control and signal. The cables supplied or recommended by the equipment manufacturer were used. In absence of any recommendation, unshielded cables were adopted, of a type appropriate for the signals involved. All cables were exposed to the magnetic field for 1m of their length. The EUT was subjected to the test magnetic field by using the induction coil of standard dimensions (1m×1m) by the immersion method. The induction coil was then be rotated by 90° in order to expose the EUT to the test field with different orientations. For floor-standing equipment the test was repeated by moving and shifting the induction coils, in order to test the whole volume of the EUT for each orthogonal direction.

The CLINICAL THERMOMETER may exhibit temporary degradation of performance (e.g. deviation from the performance indicated in the instructions for use during IMMUNITY testing), which does not require OPERATOR intervention and that does not affect BASIC SAFETY or ESSENTIAL PERFORMANCE. In the event of disruption during IMMUNITY tests, the CLINICAL THERMOMETER shall recover from any disruption within 30 s.

The following degradations, if associated with BASIC SAFETY or ESSENTIAL PERFORMANCE, shall not be allowed: component failures; changes in programmable parameters or settings; reset to default settings; change of operating mode; change in LABORATORY ACCURACY at any point in the RATED OUTPUT RANGE and in the RATED EXTENDED OUTPUT RANGE greater than permitted in 201.101.2 without the generation of either a TECHNICAL ALARM CONDITION or an indication of abnormal operation.

For a CLINICAL THERMOMETER, the following shall be considered PRIMARY OPERATING FUNCTIONS: a) observing the OUTPUT TEMPERATURE; b) properly positioning CLINICAL THERMOMETER or PROBE at the MEASURING SITE; c) starting the CLINICAL THERMOMETER from power off; d) turning off the CLINICAL THERMOMETER; e) performing a basic pre-use functional check of the CLINICAL THERMOMETER. The following functions, if available, also shall be considered PRIMARY OPERATING FUNCTIONS: f) performing a basic pre-use functional check of the ALARM SIGNALS; g) configuring the ACCESSORIES including connection of the detachable parts to the CLINICAL THERMOMETER; h) REPROCESSING the ACCESSORIES; i) setting the OPERATOR-adjustable controls: switching between MEASURING SITES; setting CLINICAL THERMOMETER control parameters; setting ALARM LIMITS; inactivating ALARM SIGNALS.

The clinical accuracy requirement is applicable only to an ear canal IR thermometer system and the corresponding age groups of subjects for which such a thermometer is labeled or implied to be used.
